name: Fast Life Yungstaz (F.L.Y.)
sources: style-research-extended vol.1 atl-swag-rap — Fast Life Yungstaz (F.L.Y.)
notes: The record that named the lane. Wikipedia files them under a "futuristic swag" subgenre "characterized by its melodious approach", and the parameters that make this entry are the two the research states as facts about the writing rather than the sound: the harmony is a tonic pedal plus at most one neighbour, and the hook is a **unison group chant on 3-5 pitches that stays inside a fifth**. That second sentence is why the countermelody here is deliberately narrow and low-density — the counter is the crowd, not a synth line, and a crowd melody has no leaps. The melodic interest is pushed the other way, into the bell/pluck MIDI loop, so `melody` carries the density and sits high. This is also the only major-leaning entry in the batch besides Roscoe Dash and K.E., and it gets there from the research's own "major-leaning and static", not from the parent's minor pool. Drums are Complex's era description taken literally — "skittering hi-hats, ringtone-inspired midi loops" gives `hihat.fillDensity` 0.56, and "no live percussion" gives a percs block with a single snap lane at [0,1] rather than the parent's three-lane offbeat kit. ⚠ `confidence` is "low" because the research rates it medium-low. Documented: the subgenre label, the roster context, the RIAA Gold certification and the producer (K.E. on the Track). INFERRED, and marked [LOW-CONF] in the research: the BPM range (68-76 half-time = 136-152), the chord numerals — the I-IV and I-V families here are this model's inferred parameter, since the research names only "a tonic pedal plus at most one neighbour chord" — and the whole 808 line ("single sustained root 808 per bar, medium decay, no slides" is era-level, hence `bass808.slideProb` 0.03 and `bassline.followRootsProb` 0.95). ⚠ `chords.impliedByRiff` is set with `maxChords` 2 because the loop genuinely is the harmony; the chord part's required variety comes from `chordDurationBeats` reaching 16, three `harmonicRhythm` values and a 32-semitone voicing register, not from progressions this record does not contain. ⚠ `transitions.dropOutBeats.prob` 0.9 over 4 beats is authored, not inherited: "full drop-out-to-vocal breaks for crowd participation — the record's afterlife as an arena chant is a structural fact about how it was built." ⚠ `anticipationProb` raised to 0.15. With `mirror_kick` against a fully locked 808 both parts take every kick, so every bass onset lands exactly on an 808 onset — `coherence.rs` calls that one line played twice rather than two parts locking. The lock is the style and is untouched; the anticipation is what makes them two parts. ⚠ **The 1-bar phrase length was removed** (was [1,2], now [2,4]). A one-bar phrase looped four times carries less entropy than a four-bar phrase, and it is the countermelody it strangles hardest: a counter answers *inside* the melody’s phrase, so a one-bar shape leaves it nowhere to go. Every worst offender on `counter.rs` carried it. ⛔ The previous session recorded this exact mistake and it arrived again from the other direction — distinctness is combinatorial in the shape LENGTH, not in the option count.
